'''Jerzy Witold Różycki''' ({{IPA|pl|ˈjɛʒɨ ruˈʒɨt͡ski|pron|Pl-Jerzy_Różycki.ogg}}; 24 July 1909 – 9 January 1942) was a Polish [[mathematician]] and [[cryptologist]] who worked at breaking German [[Enigma machine|Enigma-machine]] [[cipher]]s before and during [[World War II]].

==Life==
Różycki was born in what is now [[Ukraine]], the fourth and youngest child of Zygmunt Różycki, a pharmacist and graduate of [[Saint Petersburg University]], and Wanda, née Benita.  He attended a Polish school in [[Kyiv]] before moving with his family to Poland in 1918.  In 1926 he completed secondary school at [[Wyszków]] on eastern Poland's [[Bug River]].

Różycki studied mathematics from 1927 to 1932 in western Poland, at [[Poznań University]]'s Mathematics Institute, graduating with a master's degree on February 19, 1932.  He would later earn a second master's degree from Poznań University, in [[geography]], on December 13, 1937.

In 1929, while still a student, Różycki, proficient in [[German language|German]], was one of twenty-odd Poznań University mathematics students who accepted an invitation to attend a secret [[cryptology]] course organized at a nearby military installation by the Polish [[General Staff]]'s [[Biuro Szyfrów|Cipher Bureau]], headquartered in [[Warsaw]].

From September 1932, Różycki served as a civilian cryptologist with the [[Poland|Polish]] [[General Staff]]'s [[Biuro Szyfrów|Cipher Bureau]], housed till 1937 in [[Warsaw]]'s [[Pałac Saski|Saxon Palace]]. He worked there together with fellow [[Poznań University]] mathematics alumni and Cipher Bureau cryptology-course graduates [[Marian Rejewski]] and [[Henryk Zygalski]].

After Rejewski had reconstructed the German military [[Enigma machine]] in December 1932, Różycki and Zygalski likewise worked at ongoing development of methods and equipment to exploit Enigma [[decryption]] as a source of [[military espionage|intelligence]].  Różycki invented the "clock" method, which sometimes made it possible to determine which of the machine's [[Rotor machine|rotor]]s was at the far right, that is, in the position where the rotor always revolved at every depression of a key.
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[Image:Gralinski, Rozycki and Smolenski.jpg|thumb|300px|right|From left: [[Jan Graliński]], Jerzy Różycki and [[Piotr Smoleński]] at "[[Cadix]]" in southern France. All three perished in the 1942 ''Lamoricière'' disaster.]] -->

On 9 January 1942, Różycki perished in the [[Mediterranean Sea]] while returning to the [[Cadix]] center, near [[Uzès]] in [[Vichy France]], from a stint at Cadix's branch office at the Château Couba on the outskirts of [[Algiers]]. His passenger ship, the ''[[SS Lamoricière]]'', sank in unclear circumstances near the [[Balearic Islands]].<ref>The ship had, appropriately, been christened after a 19th-century French general, [[Christophe Léon Louis Juchault de Lamoricière]], who had been involved in the French conquest of [[Algeria]].</ref> Fellow victims of the disaster, among the 222 passengers killed, included [[Piotr Smoleński]] and Captain [[Jan Graliński]], of the prewar [[Cipher Bureau (Poland)|Polish Cipher Bureau]]'s Russian section, and a French officer accompanying the three Poles, Captain François Lane.

Różycki has a [[cenotaph]] (symbolic grave) in the National Pantheon at the [[Saints Peter and Paul Church, Kraków|Saints Peter and Paul Church]] in [[Kraków]], Poland.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://nowywyszkowiak.pl/wydarzenia/jerzy-rozycki-ma-symboliczny-grob-wyszkowianie-na-oficjalnej-uroczystosci-foto.html |title=Jerzy Różycki ma symboliczny grób. Wyszkowianie na oficjalnej uroczystości |trans-title=Jerzy Różycki has a symbolic grave. Wyszkowianie at the official ceremony |website=nowywyszkowiak.pl |access-date=29 February 2020}}</ref>

==Family==
In 1938, aged 29, Różycki married Maria Barbara Mayka. Their son, [[Janusz Różycki]], born May 10, 1939, completed his studies at the [[Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw]] and went on to be a member of the Polish [[fencing (sport)|fencing]] team that won a silver medal at the [[1964 Summer Olympics|1964 Tokyo Olympics]].

==Recognition==
[[File:2023-06-15 Cryptologist Monument Różycki.JPG|thumb|2007 monument to cryptologists [[Marian Rejewski|Rejewski]], Różycki, and [[Henryk Zygalski|Zygalski]] before the [[Imperial Castle in Poznań]]]]
In 1980 Różycki and his two mathematician colleagues were among the heroes of ''Sekret Enigmy'' (The Enigma Secret), a Polish [[Thriller (genre)|thriller film]] about their solution of the German Enigma cipher. Late 1980 also saw a similarly-themed Polish [[TV series]], ''Tajemnice Enigmy'' (The Secrets of Enigma).<ref>{{harvnb|Kasparek|Woytak|1982|p=24}}</ref>

On 21 February 2000, [[President of the Republic of Poland|Polish President]] [[Aleksander Kwaśniewski]] posthumously awarded Różycki the Grand Cross of the [[Order of Polonia Restituta]] for outstanding contributions to his homeland.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://prawo.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/DocDetails.xsp?id=WMP20000130273 |title=M.P. 2000 nr 13 poz. 273 |website=prawo.sejm.gov.pl |access-date=2019-02-25 |archive-date=2020-03-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326220042/http://prawo.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/DocDetails.xsp?id=WMP20000130273 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2007 a three-sided memorial was unveiled before the [[Imperial Castle, Poznań|Imperial Castle]] in [[Poznań]], commemorating the three mathematician-cryptologists (Rejewski, Różycki and Zygalski), alumni of the [[University of Poznań]], who reconstructed the German [[Enigma machine]] and developed methods of breaking Enigma ciphers, thus contributing to subsequent Allied victory in [[World War II]].

In 2009 the [[Polish Post]] issued a series of four commemorative stamps, one of which pictured Różycki and fellow mathematician-cryptologists [[Marian Rejewski]] and [[Henryk Zygalski]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.kzp.pl/index.php?artykul=kat-zn-2009-index |title=Znaczki z 2009 roku |trans-title=Stamps from 2009 |website=www.kzp.pl |access-date=2019-02-25}}</ref>

On 5 August 2014 the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) posthumously honored Rejewski, Różycki, and Zygalski with its Milestone Award, given for "First Breaking of Enigma Code by the Team of Polish Cipher Bureau, 1932-1939". The three had built the '[[Bomba (cryptography)|bomba]]' – the first cryptanalytic machine to break codes. Their work was a foundation of British code breaking efforts which, with later American assistance, helped end World War II.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ieeer10.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/IEEE-R10-Newsletter_Dec2014.pdf |title=IEEE R10 News and Highlights |website=www.ieeer10.org |access-date=2019-02-25}}</ref>
In 2014 a commemorative plaque in Polish and English, dedicated to Różycki and his two colleagues, was unveiled before the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] Mathematics Institute in [[Warsaw]].

In 2018 a bench commemorating Różycki was unveiled in a park in the town of [[Wyszków]], where Różycki had attended secondary school.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://nowywyszkowiak.pl/wydarzenia/na-laweczce-obok-rozyckiego-foto.html |title=Na ławeczce obok Różyckiego |trans-title=On the bench next to Różycki |website=nowywyszkowiak.pl |access-date=2019-02-25}}</ref>

In 2021 the [[Enigma Cipher Centre]], an educational and scientific institution dedicated to the Polish mathematicians who broke the Enigma cipher, including Jerzy Różycki, opened in Poznań.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thefirstnews.com/article/new-centre-dedicated-to-polish-enigma-codebreakers-opens-in-poznan-24926 |title=New centre dedicated to Polish Enigma codebreakers opens in Poznań |website=www.thefirstnews.com |access-date=25 September 2021 |archive-date=24 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924195148/https://www.thefirstnews.com/article/new-centre-dedicated-to-polish-enigma-codebreakers-opens-in-poznan-24926 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
